stories.title: Extell Finalizes Deal to Buy 110 East 55th Street for $65M
stories.excerpt: After months of negotiations, Extell Development has acquired 110 East 55th Street, a 19-story Midtown office property also known as Park 55, from the Parkoff Organization for $65 million, property records made public Monday show. An affiliate of construction company JT Magen — which had previously partnered with Extell on a foreclosure in Boston — filed a pre-foreclosure suit at the property in May, The Real Deal reported. The foreclosure complaint alleged that Parkoff defaulted on a loan and owed some $40.6 million in principal and interest. Parkoff and Extell did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. Extell founder Gary Barnett was reported to be in contract for the property back in January, but a sales price was never reported until the deal closed this week. Now, Barnett will add the building to his firm’s ever-growing collection of Midtown-based assets. Most recently, Extell acquired a block-long development site at 405-417 Park Avenue in May for $500 million, CO previously reported. The site — which has the potential for upwards of 700,000 square feet of rentable office space — went up for sale in August of last year. Extell also acquired the Friars Club building at 57 East 55th Street for $19 million in late April. Additionally, Barnett secured 123,000 square feet of air rights over Saint Thomas Church at 678 Fifth Avenue for $36 million last year. It’s unclear exactly what Barnett has planned for his massive Midtown assemblage — which is also set to include 111 East 54th Street — but the developer is already busy with other development projects in Manhattan. The firm has several Midtown developments in the works, including a 600-foot-tall office tower at 570 Fifth Avenue, a 1,200-foot residential tower at 77 West 66th Street, a 70-story condominium at 50 West 66th Street, a 71-story mixed-use tower at 871 Seventh Avenue — the former Wellington Hotel — and a 1,162-foot-tall residential skyscraper at 655 Madison Avenue. bullets: Extell acquires 110 East 55th Street (19-story Midtown office) for $65M from foreclosure.
Property originated from $40.6M defaulted loan; Extell now owns multiple Midtown assets including 405-417 Park Avenue ($500M, May 2025).
Signals distressed office-to-mixed-use conversion opportunity in prime Manhattan submarkets.
stories.summary: Extell Development closed acquisition of 110 East 55th Street, a 19-story Midtown Manhattan office building, for $65 million from Parkoff Organization following a foreclosure action. The property had carried a $40.6 million principal and interest default. This addition to Extell's Midtown portfolio follows the firm's $500 million acquisition of 405-417 Park Avenue in May 2025, signaling aggressive land accumulation by a major NYC developer.
stories.impact: Distressed office assets in prime Manhattan submarkets remain acquisition targets for well-capitalized developers with conversion optionality (residential, mixed-use). Extell's scale and repeated Midtown acquisitions suggest confidence in future residential demand and/or zoning flexibility that justifies near-term office hold; closely watch approval timelines for conversions and residential entitlements on these sites, as they may indicate where rental demand is expected to support new supply in Midtown East/Central.

stories.title: Chipotle, Starbucks to Open at Pullman Gateway Complex
stories.excerpt: Pullman Gateway has achieved full occupancy, completing the transformation of a long-vacant property into a mixed-use destination developed and fully leased in just over two years. The grand opening of a 1,500-square-foot Chipotle Mexican Grill with a drive-thru at 11211 South Corliss Avenue marks the completion of the eight-acre development. The celebration also marked the announcement of another major commercial investment in the community. Plans call for the new Pullman Park Retail Center, a commercial development anchored by Starbucks, Tropical Smoothie Café, and Slim & Husky’s Pizza Beeria. Slim & Husky’s will be the Nashville-based pizza company’s first Chicago location, with former Chicago Bear Matt Forte as a significant investor.Together, Pullman Gateway and the new Pullman Park Retail Center, developed by Chicago Neighborhood Initiatives, represent the next phase of sustained investment. Located at 112th Street and South Corliss Avenue, Pullman Gateway has transformed a former Hawthorne Racecourse off-track betting facility and underutilized parking lot into a mixed-use development featuring Chick-fil-A, Dunkin’ and Jimmy John’s, along with CTA offices supporting construction of the Red Line Extension. The post Chipotle, Starbucks to Open at Pullman Gateway Complex appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Pullman Gateway (Chicago, 8-acre mixed-use) achieves full occupancy; Chipotle, Starbucks anchor tenants.
Second phase Pullman Park Retail Center announced with Starbucks, Slim & Husky's (Nashville pizza brand's first Chicago location).
Converted vacant Hawthorne Racetrack site into leased mixed-use destination in 2+ years.
stories.summary: Pullman Gateway, an 8-acre mixed-use development on Chicago's South Side, achieved full occupancy with opening of a 1,500-sf Chipotle with drive-thru. A second phase, Pullman Park Retail Center, is planned with anchors including Starbucks and Slim & Husky's Pizza Beeria (Nashville firm's first Chicago location, backed by former Chicago Bear Matt Forte). The project represents transformation of the long-vacant Hawthorne Racetrack site.
stories.impact: Successful conversion of distressed/underutilized land in secondary Chicago submarkets (South Side) signals housing and retail demand sufficient to justify rapid lease-up. The pace (2+ years to full occupancy) and anchor tenant quality (QSR/national brands) indicate improving South Side fundamentals; multifamily developers should monitor adjacent neighborhoods for demographic/employment drivers that may underpin new residential supply absorption in the broader Pullman/South Side corridor.

stories.title: Co-Working Provider Canopy Signs Full-Building Lease at Long-Vacant Presidio Structure
stories.excerpt: The Presidio Trust has signed a 40,000-square-foot lease with Canopy, a boutique co-working and flexible office provider, for the full building at 102 Montgomery St. It is the last historic brick structure on the Presidio’s Main Post to be restored and activated, and one of the largest leases signed in the San Francisco landmark complex this year. Originally constructed in 1896, the building had been vacant since the 1970s. Following an 18-month, full-scale rehabilitation by the Trust, the property has been brought back to life for modern use. The new Canopy location, which joins three others in San Francisco, is expected to open in the spring of 2027. “We’re very pleased to welcome CANOPY to the Presidio,” said Daryl Ansel, interim director of commercial asset management, Presidio Trust. “Creating places where people can work, connect, and engage with the park strengthens the Presidio’s vitality and supports a dynamic tenant community.” The post Co-Working Provider Canopy Signs Full-Building Lease at Long-Vacant Presidio Structure appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Canopy (boutique co-working) signs 40,000-sf full-building lease at 102 Montgomery St, Presidio, San Francisco.
Historic 1896 structure vacant since 1970s; 18-month restoration by Presidio Trust; opens spring 2027.
One of largest Presidio Main Post leases this year; Canopy's fourth San Francisco location.
stories.summary: The Presidio Trust signed a full-building, 40,000-square-foot lease with Canopy, a boutique co-working provider, for 102 Montgomery Street. The 1896 brick structure had been vacant since the 1970s and underwent an 18-month full restoration. The property is Canopy's fourth San Francisco location and one of the largest leases on the Presidio's Main Post this year, with opening slated for spring 2027.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily development. Co-working lease signals ongoing San Francisco demand for flexible workspace (not residential), though the Presidio's historic-adaptive-reuse profile and mixed-use activation may indirectly support demand for nearby housing. No clear multifamily supply or demand signal.

stories.title: CBRE Arranges Sale of Apartment Buildings in Wisconsin
stories.excerpt: CBRE has arranged the sale of Riverwood Apartments, a fully occupied 32-unit multifamily community in Mauston, Wisconsin. Tripp & Associates acquired the property from Riverwood Apartments, LLC for $3.95 million. CBRE’s Sean Beuche, Max Colby, Matson Holbrook and Gretchen Richards represented the seller in the transaction. “Mauston has proven to be a compelling market for multifamily investment,” said Beuche. “The growing employment base includes full-service healthcare, manufacturers expanding their operations and significant regional tourism drawn from Wisconsin Dells, which is just 23 minutes away.” Riverwood Apartments includes four two-story residential buildings on 3.24 acres along the Lemonweir River. Built in 1994, the property offers a mix of one-, two- and three-bedroom floor plans with units ranging from 575 to 1,000 square feet. “Smaller Wisconsin markets like Mauston are where the supply-demand imbalance is most evident,” said Joan Tripicchio, Principal, Tripp & Associates. bullets: Tripp & Associates acquires Riverwood Apartments (32-unit, fully occupied) in Mauston, Wisconsin for $3.95M.
Built 1994; 1-, 2-, 3-bedroom mix; 3.24 acres along Lemonweir River; CBRE represented seller.
Broker cites employment growth (healthcare, manufacturing), regional tourism (Wisconsin Dells 23 min away) and supply-demand imbalance in smaller Wisconsin markets.
stories.summary: CBRE arranged the sale of Riverwood Apartments, a fully occupied 32-unit community in Mauston, Wisconsin, to Tripp & Associates for $3.95 million. The 1994-built property sits on 3.24 acres and offers one-, two-, and three-bedroom units (575–1,000 sf). Sellers' broker highlighted Mauston's employment base expansion (healthcare, manufacturing) and proximity to Wisconsin Dells (23 minutes) as demand drivers.
stories.impact: Tight multifamily supply in smaller Wisconsin markets (Mauston) is driving investor acquisition of stabilized, fully occupied assets at low absolute prices, signaling limited new-build pipeline and sustained rental demand in secondary/tertiary metros. For Trammell Crow, this flags opportunity to identify and develop new supply in underserved Midwest towns with employer growth (healthcare, manufacturing) and tourism nearby before supply tightens further and cap rates compress.

stories.title: Marcus & Millichap Brokers Sale of 31-Unit Multifamily Near Kansas City
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap completed the sale of Creekside Village, a 31-unit multifamily property in Grain Valley, Missouri. “Creekside Village attracted significant investor interest because of its location in one of the Kansas City area’s fastest-growing suburban markets,” said Jacob Carroll, associate director of investments. Carroll and Aaron Kuroiwa, investment specialists in Marcus & Millichap’s Kansas City and Indianapolis offices, had the exclusive listing to market the property on behalf of the seller, Creekside SPE – Apartments, LLC, and procured the buyer, a Kansas City-based investor.  Creekside Village Apartments is situated on 1.21 acres at 900 N.E. Deer Creek Road. Built in 2007, the property features 31 one- and two-bedroom units across 28,055 rentable square feet. Located approximately 25 minutes east of downtown Kansas City, the community is near major retail, dining and recreational amenities. If you’re reading about the multifamily industry, you should be in the room with its leaders. Connect Apartments brings together the executives featured in Connect CRE’s coverage for an afternoon of high-level insights and unmatched networking on September 22 at The Biltmore in LA. The post Marcus & Millichap Brokers Sale of 31-Unit Multifamily Near Kansas City appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Marcus & Millichap sells Creekside Village (31-unit, 2007-built) in Grain Valley, Missouri for undisclosed price.
Located 25 min east of downtown Kansas City near retail/dining; 1-, 2-bedroom units in one of area's fastest-growing suburban markets.
Kansas City-based buyer; broker cited significant investor interest in Kansas City suburban markets.
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap completed the sale of Creekside Village, a 31-unit multifamily property in Grain Valley, Missouri (approximately 25 minutes east of downtown Kansas City), to a Kansas City-based investor. Built in 2007, the community features one- and two-bedroom units across 28,055 rentable square feet on 1.21 acres. The sale drew significant investor interest due to the property's location in one of the Kansas City area's fastest-growing suburban markets.
stories.impact: Kansas City suburban markets (Grain Valley, east of downtown) are attracting multifamily investor capital and characterized as fast-growing. Monitor job and population growth drivers (corporate expansions, highway/transit projects) in Kansas City suburbs to time new development ahead of supply shortfalls; stabilized asset sales at solid fundamentals may indicate rising rents and entry yields that justify new starts.

stories.title: Terreno Realty Acquires Red Hook Warehouse for $26M
stories.excerpt: Terreno Realty has acquired a warehouse along the Red Hook, Brooklyn, waterfront. Terreno announced Monday the purchase of the 28,000-square-foot industrial property at 659 Court Street for $26.3 million from California-based LBA Properties, which made a pretty penny since buying it less thana year and a half ago for $7 million, according to property records. The building sits right on the banks of the East River with parking for 70 cars and two loading bays, according to the buyers. The warehouse is also leased to a maritime goods and services provider. It’s unclear who brokered the deal. LBA did not immediately respond to a request for comment, while Terreno did not immediately respond to a request for additional comment. With 145,800 square feet of buildable space with the addition of air rights, the price for the property has fluctuated dramatically over the years. Buckeye Partners, which sold the property to LBA in March 2025, acquired it themselves in 2013 for $15.5 million, but paid $92.1 million in a real property transfer tax in late 2019, according to property records. The transaction follows on strong leasing fundamentals reported in the industrial sector in the second quarter of 2026. CBRE clocked leasing at an 11 percent increase year-over-year to 268.7 million square feet across the U.S., while vacancies dropped to 6.5 percent, according to the report. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Terreno Realty acquires Red Hook (Brooklyn) waterfront warehouse for $26.3M; 28,000 sf at 659 Court Street.
LBA Properties sold for 3.7x gain (bought $7M, ~18 months ago); property leased to maritime services provider.
Includes 145,800 sf buildable with air rights; property appreciated materially in <2 years despite industrial sector volatility.
stories.summary: Terreno Realty acquired a 28,000-square-foot waterfront industrial warehouse at 659 Court Street in Red Hook, Brooklyn, for $26.3 million. The property, leased to a maritime goods and services provider, offers 70-car parking and two loading bays. Seller LBA Properties purchased it less than 18 months prior for $7 million, realizing a substantial gain. The site includes 145,800 square feet of buildable space with air rights.
stories.impact: Waterfront industrial assets in Brooklyn continue to command premium pricing and rapid appreciation, driven by scarcity, last-mile logistics demand, and conversion optionality. However, this is an industrial/logistics play, not multifamily. Red Hook's neighborhood-level gentrification (restaurants, creative tenants) may eventually support residential upside, but no direct signal on apartment demand or supply here.

We have definitely seen a significant increase in the number of requests for outdoor storage and have so far been lukewarm to the asset class until we can develop a better understanding of the business and long-term viability. The re-use is easy, but that entails a significant decrease in the value that the deal was originally done at. bullets: Red Oak Capital Holdings (industrial lender) reports consistent industrial borrowing demand; no shift in product types year-over-year.
Single-, multi-tenant, light manufacturing, flex remain steady; significant increase in outdoor storage requests but lender cautious on long-term viability.
Industrial debt market stable; no material compression in borrower appetite or collateral profiles.
stories.summary: David Christensen, regional manager for Red Oak Capital Holdings, reports that industrial borrowing demand remains consistent with prior year, with stable requests for single-tenant, multi-tenant, light manufacturing, and flex assets. The firm has seen a significant increase in outdoor storage inquiries but remains cautious on the asset class's long-term viability and re-use economics. The comments suggest steady industrial lending conditions on the West Coast.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily development. Industrial debt stability and product-type consistency suggest no construction cost shocks or financing availability crises on the West Coast, which indirectly supports multifamily cap rates and borrowing. No supply or demand signal specific to apartments.

stories.title: Aircraft Finance Firm Buys Florida HQ Complex For $118M
stories.excerpt: A publicly traded aircraft finance firm has paid $118 million for a three-building, 375,000-square-foot campus under construction in Coconut Creek, Fla. disclosed the transaction and purchase price in a public filing this month. The Coconut Creek-based company bought Cocomar Business Park, under development at 4733, 4763 and 4851 West Atlantic Boulevard as its new corporate headquarters, the South Florida Business Journal reported. The company lists its current headquarters as 4700 Lyons Technology Parkway. The seller is an affiliate of Greystar of Charleston, S.C., which last year bought the site for $30.5 million. A marketing brochure said the industrial buildings include 32-foot ceilings, 78 dock doors and 313 parking spaces. Each building includes a small amount of office space and conference rooms. Completion of the 35-acre campus is expected in the third quarter of this year. In its most recent annual report, Willis Lease Finance said it owns its 60,000-square-foot headquarters in Coconut Creek and leases 45,000 square feet in Pompano Beach, Fla., and 25,000 square feet in Sunrise, Fla. The company reported 475 employees in the U.S., the United Kingdom, Ireland and elsewhere. As of the end of 2025, Willis Lease Finance owned 363 engines, 20 aircraft, one marine vessel and other leased parts and equipment leased out to 69 lessees in 37 countries. Jeff Ostrowski can be reached at jostrowski@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Willis Lease Finance (aircraft finance, public) buys Cocomar Business Park (3-building, 375,000 sf, under construction) in Coconut Creek, Florida for $118M.
Property serves as company's new HQ; built by Greystar, acquired for $30.5M in 2024; completion Q3 2025.
32-ft ceilings, 78 dock doors, 313 parking; 35-acre campus; tenant company consolidates from two current Florida locations.
stories.summary: Willis Lease Finance Corporation, a publicly traded aircraft finance firm, purchased Cocomar Business Park—a three-building, 375,000-square-foot industrial/office campus under construction in Coconut Creek, Florida—for $118 million to serve as its new corporate headquarters. Developed by Greystar (acquired for $30.5 million in 2024), the 35-acre campus is expected to complete in Q3 2025. The property features 32-foot ceilings, 78 dock doors, and 313 parking spaces.
stories.impact: Corporate headquarters consolidation in South Florida (Willis Lease consolidating from Coconut Creek and Pompano Beach into single Cocomar campus) may reduce office/industrial demand in the region near-term but signals business confidence in South Florida. The $118M valuation on a purpose-built industrial/office campus indicates strong cap rates and investor appetite in Broward County. No direct multifamily signal, but strengthening corporate presence in Coconut Creek/West Broward may eventually support residential demand if employer headcount grows.

stories.title: PGIM Sells Delray Beach Assisted Living Community for at Least $140M
stories.excerpt: PGIM Real Estate sold a relatively new assisted living facility in Delray Beach, Fla., for at least $140 million, marking one of the biggest South Florida retirement home sales in recent years. Chevy Chase, Md.-based Artemis Real Estate Partners purchased the 7.2-acre asset, property records show. The 224,951-square-foot community, called The Arbor at Delray, houses 207 apartments at 6595 Morikami Park Road, just west of South Jog Road. The complex includes a 35,586-square-foot recreational clubhouse and a 51,461-square-foot nursing home. The sale breaks down to just under $676,300 per unit, though it’s unclear whether the $140 million figure listed on the deed also includes the operations for the business, which could boost the price tag. PGIM Real Estate, part of insurance giant Prudential Financial, completed the property in 2023. Two years earlier, PGIM-backed Alliance Residential Company purchased the land for $8.2 million and secured a $45.7 million construction loan from Dallas-based Comerica Bank, The Real Deal reported. There’s been an uptick in the number of assisted living facilities across Palm Beach County this year as the occupancy rate in Florida neared 90 percent, with monthly rents averaging over $5,000 in the second quarter of 2026, according to data from Colliers. Just last week, Healthpeak Properties bought a 136-unit facility in Boynton Beach for at least $62 million. Representatives for Artemis and PGIM did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: PGIM Real Estate sells The Arbor at Delray (207-unit assisted living community, 224,951 sf) to Artemis Real Estate Partners for ≥$140M.
New property completed 2023; $676K+ per unit; includes 35,586-sf clubhouse and 51,461-sf nursing home; 7.2 acres at 6595 Morikami Park Road.
PGIM-backed Alliance Residential purchased land for $8.2M in 2021; $45.7M construction loan from Comerica Bank.
stories.summary: PGIM Real Estate sold The Arbor at Delray, a recently completed (2023) assisted living community in Delray Beach, Florida, to Chevy Chase-based Artemis Real Estate Partners for at least $140 million. The 7.2-acre property comprises 207 assisted-living apartments (224,951 sf total), a 35,586-square-foot recreational clubhouse, and a 51,461-square-foot nursing home, representing approximately $676,300 per unit. PGIM's underlying company purchased the land in 2021 for $8.2 million and secured a $45.7 million construction loan.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to market-rate multifamily. Senior-housing asset appreciation (land $8.2M → $140M sale in ~4 years) signals strong Delray Beach real estate fundamentals, investor appetite for age-restricted communities, and favorable financing conditions in 2021–2023. However, assisted living is a specialized nursing/care asset class, not standard apartments. Monitor Delray's overall residential demand (55+ population, median age, in-migration) as a proxy for broader South Florida housing market health, but this transaction does not signal apartment supply or demand directly.

stories.title: Mamdani Invests $8.4M in Business Improvement Districts Citywide
stories.excerpt: Mayor Zohran Mamdani is upping the grant funding available to local organizations that promote commerce — though it doesn’t look like much. Mamdani and the New York City Department of Small Business Services (SBS) is making $8.4 million available to business improvement districts for public art displays, street cleaning, lighting and directories. While $8.4 million might not be the most impressive figure, the administration says it could boost foot traffic for 20,000 businesses in the five boroughs, and is the largest single cash infusion of its kind. “Our administration knows it’s not enough to make it easier to open a small business, you have to make it easier to visit one, too,” Mamdani said in a statement. “That’s why our commitment to small businesses means not only cutting red tape and reducing fines, but investing in the neighborhoods surrounding bodegas, bookshops and restaurants so that New York City is lined with ‘OPEN’ signs year-round.” The grant money has already been awarded, with Brooklyn taking the majority of available funding, or $2.7 million for 32 organizations, while 17 entities in the Bronx received $1.55 million, according to the administration. Manhattan and Queens received similar amounts, while the Bronx saw less funding and Staten Island got the least: $550,000 to only seven organizations. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: NYC Mayor Mamdani allocates $8.4M in grants to business improvement districts (BIDs) citywide for public art, street cleaning, lighting, directories.
Funds said to support 20,000 businesses; largest single-grant infusion of its kind; Brooklyn received majority allocation.
Initiative aims to boost foot traffic and keep storefronts 'OPEN' amid ongoing retail/small-business challenges.
stories.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and the Department of Small Business Services announced $8.4 million in grant funding to business improvement districts across the five boroughs for public art, street cleaning, lighting, and directories. The administration claims the investment could boost foot traffic for 20,000 businesses and represents the largest single cash infusion to BIDs in the city's history. Brooklyn received the majority of the allocation.
stories.impact: Indirect signal on NYC neighborhood stabilization and mixed-use investment climate. Public realm improvements (street cleaning, lighting, art) and foot-traffic goals suggest city is prioritizing neighborhood vitality and commercial street activation, which can support demand for ground-floor retail in multifamily developments and increase density/walkscore appeal of residential sites. However, $8.4M is modest and does not materially change multifamily underwriting or supply/demand dynamics. May marginally improve entitlement and zoning support for mixed-use development in BID-covered neighborhoods, but no direct signal on apartment rents, supply, or financing.
